stem: Rohan is doing an experiment at home to find out what makes a puri puff up while frying. He changes the temperature of the oil and the amount of oil used each time. Which set of evidence should he observe or measure to make sense of the changes in his experiment?

options.text: Only the amount of oil he added each time
Whatever he can remember after the experiment is over
The temperature of the oil, the amount of oil used, and whether each puri puffed up
Nothing, because whether a puri puffed is only a yes/no observation

teacher.key_rationale: Good evidence combines measurable quantities (oil temperature, amount of oil) with observable outcomes, including yes/no observations like whether the puri puffed. A omits the outcome and records only what was changed; B relies on memory instead of notes taken during the experiment; D wrongly rejects yes/no observations as evidence.
